conflicts.fact: Which lesson addresses 'how does the body avoid digesting itself' and when it was covered
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says this question will be revisited in Lesson 6 (overview) but also in Lesson 5 (DQB phase). Lesson 5 only raises it as a new question; Lesson 6 actually answers it.

conflicts.fact: Number and identity of food samples in the food test practical, and what is tested in Lesson 4 vs 5
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says 'five food samples' (ugali cooked and raw, banana, sukuma wiki extract, glucose control), which is five items but lists 'five labelled test tubes'. Lesson 5 says that Lesson 4 confirmed starch in ugali and reducing sugars in ripe banana, and that sukuma wiki is the sample with a faint emulsion. Lesson 4 says nothing about the fat/protein tests, consistent. Lesson 5 says Benedict/iodine results existed for sukuma wiki as weak/negative.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the sequence / lesson counts and reference to cumulative model start
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says the cumulative diagram was built 'since Lesson 2', while Lessons 3 and 6 say it began in Lesson 1. Lesson 8 says 'eight lessons investigating' vs 'over seven lessons' in its own overview.

conflicts.fact: Number of enzymes/regions pepsin works on and the stomach enzymes
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 lists only pepsin and HCl as stomach chemical agents; Lesson 3 adds rennin as a stomach protein-digesting enzyme, which is not mentioned elsewhere (Lesson 8 does not include rennin).

conflicts.fact: How the body 'knows' which chemical to release at each stage
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 explains it as sphincters acting as mechanical gatekeepers coordinating timing; Lesson 3 explains it as specific glands secreting specific enzymes at specific locations; Lesson 7 says cells are genetically programmed to respond to food stimuli; Lesson 8 says it is hormonal and neural signals.

conflicts.fact: Which fat enzyme and absorbed enzymes, and where protein/fat digestion described
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says protein digestion takes longer because stomach acid must activate pepsinogen; Lesson 8 says it is because of complex sequential action of pepsin, trypsin and chymotrypsin. Lesson 5 says fat digestion is the delayed one.
